paragraphs: On Tuesday morning, Tom and Ben waited at the school crossing. The cars were fast, and the crossing was too short. Tom looked at Ben's feet, and he saw new white trainers. "Nice trainers," said Tom. "Thanks," said Ben. "I need them for PE today." "What is our timetable today?" asked Tom. "Math at half past eight, science at ten, and PE after lunch," said Ben.

The light turned green, and the boys crossed the road. "Did you do the homework for Teacher Nick?" asked Ben. "Not yet," said Tom. "I have to write an article for the school newsletter." "What is it about?" asked Ben. "It is about this crossing," said Tom. "It is too short, and many students run." "That is a good idea," said Ben, "but you must finish it by Friday." "I know," said Tom. "I will study in the library at lunch."

They walked through the school gate and past the sports field. "Do you want to go skating on Saturday?" asked Tom. "No, thanks," said Ben. "I don't go skating anymore." Tom was surprised. "Why not? You love skating," he said. "I loved it last year," said Ben, "but now I play volleyball every Saturday." "Come and play, too," said Ben. "It is easy to learn."

At lunch, the boys met in the library, and they sat at a table near the window. Tom opened his notebook and read the first line of his article. "The school crossing has a problem," he read. "Add a number," said Ben. "How many students cross it every morning?" "I think two hundred," said Tom. "Then write that," said Ben. "Make the sentences short, because younger students read the newsletter, too." Tom wrote for twenty minutes, and Ben read each line and fixed two words.

After lunch, they had PE, and Ben wore his new trainers. "Are they good for running?" asked Tom. "Yes," said Ben, "and I ran very fast!" On Friday, Tom gave his article to Teacher Nick. Teacher Nick read it in the corridor, and he smiled. "A short crossing is a real problem," he said. "I will talk to the school office." Tom was very happy.
text.summary: Tom and Ben talk about their timetable, their homework, and Saturday on the way to school. Tom writes an article about the short school crossing, and Ben helps him.
